# Live fixtures — captured 2026-08-27

Read-only GETs against `https://api.staging.conduit.financial/v2` (the environment the current key is scoped to; user-confirmed isolated/synthetic). Requirements payloads were previously verified identical in shape to the real sandbox. Recapture with `./recapture.sh` (same curl calls) whenever `schemaVersion` bumps or a form e2e breaks.

Also carries `fundedBy: []`, which the list response omits |

Note on all `payout_requirements_*` fixtures: top-level `whitelist {required}`, `documentation {required, acceptedDocumentTypes}`, `blockedJurisdictions` are route-gating metadata — the app reads these, never hardcodes gating rules.

EUR virtual accounts: **this is a per-organization runtime fact, and the two hosts disagree.** On `api.sandbox.conduit.financial` (verified live 2026-08-28, full-verification run) the EUR arm is **open**: `features/requirements?asset=EUR` answers 200, the feature application is approved, and the account activates — `virtual_account_live_eur.json` is that account. The refusal below is the **staging** org and still stands there. Discovery's `/asset/code` allowedValues is `["EUR","USD"]`, and the EUR request 422s `NO_ELIGIBLE_PROVIDER` on the staging org — availability is a runtime provider check, not a schema fact. **Re-verified live 2026-08-28:** still 422, still `NO_ELIGIBLE_PROVIDER`, and the body carries `title`, `detail`, `resolution` and `correlationId` — the four things the error card renders. Raise org EUR coverage with Conduit; the app handles the refusal either way, so this is an earlier round gate's EUR arm.

**Feature requirements are per customer, not per organization (found 2026-08-28):** `feature_requirements_virtual_account_usd.json` has `minDocuments: 0`, but the same call for a customer without an active account answered `minDocuments: 1`. The console reads the number off each customer's own response and shows the upload widget when it is non-zero — never assume the fixture's zero.

**Conversions run end to end on the sandbox org (verified 2026-08-28, full-verification run).** With a USD *and* a EUR virtual account on one customer, `POST /v2/quotes` → `POST /v2/orders` → `POST /v2/orders/{id}/execute` reaches **`succeeded`** with no simulator at all — the sandbox settles the conversion itself in ~15 s, emitting `order.created`, `transaction.created`, `transaction.completed` and `order.succeeded`. There is no "conversion succeeded" simulator to call: `/v2/sandbox/orders/{id}/simulate/*` offers only `conversion-failed`, `rate-lock-expired` and `cosign`, all negative or crypto paths. The paragraph below describes the **staging** org, where the arm is still closed.

**Conversions price live, but cannot be ordered on the staging org (found 2026-08-28, live).** `POST /v2/quotes` answers **both** directions — USD→EUR and EUR→USD, 200, one option each, rate and spread populated. `POST /v2/orders` cannot follow, because a `QuoteRedemptionOrderDto` names two virtual accounts and this organization holds **USD only** (same `NO_ELIGIBLE_PROVIDER` wall as the EUR arm). The only pair the console can name is therefore same-asset, which Conduit refuses by design: `422 INVALID_ORDER_COMBO`, *"fiat same-asset moves are not orderable; use /payouts"* — a correct answer, and the documented limit of an earlier round gate's conversion arm. Order **execute**, **cancel** and the two sandbox order simulators are unreachable for the same reason; their wire bodies are asserted against stubs in `tests/test_web_convert.py`. Getting the real arm needs an org with EUR virtual-account coverage.

**A conversion option carries no rail (same run):** `options[].rail` is `null` on both directions — a fiat-to-fiat conversion has no payment rail. The panel renders the em dash `payments.quote_view` substitutes, and the stub fixture (`tests/payments_fixtures.py::CONVERSION_QUOTE`) matches live rather than inventing one. Note also the interaction with `lockSide: source`: a 1000.00 lock converts **999.00** and debits **1000.00** — the fee comes out of the locked amount, so `sourceAmount` and `totalDebit` differ and the confirm screen shows both.

**Sandbox order surface (read 2026-08-28 from `https://api.sandbox.conduit.financial/v2/api-docs/openapi.json`, read-only, nothing pinned):** for a fiat conversion the order-scoped simulators are `POST /v2/sandbox/orders/{id}/simulate/conversion-failed` and `…/simulate/rate-lock-expired` (both take an empty JSON object). `…/simulate/cosign` is the non-custodial crypto signing leg and is deliberately not wired. Settlement of the resulting `fiat_conversion` transaction is `POST /v2/sandbox/transactions/{id}/simulate/terminal` `{outcome}` — the payout simulators (`simulate-review-*`, `simulate/settled`) are withdrawal-shaped and do not apply.

Missing on purpose (can't be captured read-only): a live `OrderExternalResponseDto` — see the paragraph above; it needs an org that can hold two currencies. The `422 ONBOARDING_NOT_READY` body was captured 2026-08-28 by `tests/e2e/02_onboarding.py`; re-run that script (write calls, staging) to refresh it.

**Discovery defect (found 2026-08-28, live):** `POST /v2/onboarding` requires `ownership.persons[].address.{country,addressLine1,city,state,postalCode}` — `422 ONBOARDING_NOT_READY`, "Country is required", "Street 1 is required", … — but `individualRequirements[].fields` declares no `address` pointer in any of the four country fixtures, and `OnboardingSubmitDto` documents only "roles[], scalar identity fields, and documentIds[]". `forms._person_address` works around it by copying the payload's own `registeredAddress` block under the person; it turns itself off the moment discovery declares one. Raise with Conduit alongside the other filed issues.

**Discovery/API mismatch (same run):** `individualRequirements[0].role` is `"any"`, but submitting `roles: ["any"]` is rejected — `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, *"Invalid role \"any\". Allowed: BENEFICIAL_OWNER, CONTROLLING_PERSON, LEGAL_REPRESENTATIVE"*. The row's `role` is a requirement selector, not a role value; `forms.person_roles` takes the person's own `/roles` answer instead (FORM_ENGINE_SPEC §5.4, corrected).

**Discovery defect — CONFIRMED SPURIOUS (found 2026-08-28, verified live 2026-08-28):** both fedwire payout fixtures declare `destination.ach.authorizationType` with `required: true` — an ACH-subtree field on a fedwire route (sepa/swift fixtures do not do this). A live fedwire payout carrying `destination.ach.authorizationType: "corporate_agreement"` was **accepted (202) and the whole `ach` subtree silently dropped** — it does not appear on the created resource (`payout_live_withdrawal.json`). So the field is neither validated nor stored on this rail: harmless, but it makes the console ask an operator a mandatory question that changes nothing. Filed as conduit-issues/06.

This is the **one place the console overrides discovery** (`payments._spurious_ach`): `destination.ach.*` fields are hidden when the route's rail is not `ach`, so they reach neither the form nor the assembled body. A genuine ACH route keeps them untouched. Everywhere else the engine still obeys the requirements response verbatim (FORM_ENGINE_SPEC §1); delete the override the day discovery stops declaring the subtree off-rail — the rail check already makes it a no-op on ACH.

**Discovery/spec enum-casing mismatch (found 2026-08-28, live):** discovery declares `destination.recipient.accountType` as `["CHECKING","SAVINGS"]` and `destination.recipient.type` as `["BUSINESS"]`, while `FiatPayoutDto` in the pinned OpenAPI declares both **lowercase** (`checking|savings`, `business|individual`). Conduit accepts the uppercase form discovery advertises and normalises it: the created payout reads back `accountType: "checking"`, `type: "business"`. The engine emits discovery's verbatim key (FORM_ENGINE_SPEC §3), which is the correct rule and works — but the two documents disagree and only one of them can be right.

**Undeclared field filled in by Conduit (same run):** the created payout carries `destination.recipient.rail: "us"`, which discovery never declares and the console never sends. It is inferred from the payout rail. (The Phase-0 `money.sh` probe had to send `recipient.rail` by hand; that is no longer necessary.)

**`evidenceDocumentIds` is required *and* non-empty (found 2026-08-28, live):** `POST /customers/{id}/whitelist-recipients` with `evidenceDocumentIds: []` answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, pointer `/evidenceDocumentIds`, *"Too small: expected array to have >=1 items"* — on a `relationship: self` registration, which the DTO's own prose ("evidencing the intercompany relationship") reads as though it would exempt. The console therefore requires at least one evidence document on every registration (`payments.EVIDENCE_MIN`). The schema declares only `required`, not `minItems`; raise with Conduit.

**`POST /v2/quotes` refuses `Idempotency-Key` (found 2026-08-28, live):** `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` — *"Idempotency-Key is not supported on this endpoint — a replay always reprices, so caching a response here would…"*. This is the **one known exception** to OPERATIONS_SPEC §5's "send it unconditionally, verified live"; the console's quote route sends none, and a quote is not ledgered (it creates nothing).

**Staging cannot complete a payout cancellation (found 2026-08-28, live):** `POST /v2/payouts/{id}/cancel` immediately after creation answers `409 PAYOUT_CANCEL_IN_PROGRESS` ("was just created; retry the cancellation"); a retry ~10s later answers `200`. But the payout then parks at `status: pending`, `stage: under_review` and never reaches `cancelled` — staging has no `/v2/sandbox/*` route to resolve the compliance review, and no RFI is raised against it. Two ZZZTEST payouts of $11.00 are stranded in that state from an earlier round e2e (`txn_034F7vDOR513OWlb4h2jWp`, `txn_034F81CcYqCVgifODldDwt`). **Because of this the e2e's payout-create leg is opt-in — `E2E_CREATE_PAYOUT=1`, default off** — so a routine run cannot accumulate one per invocation; requirements, quote and whitelist legs stay always-on. The console behaves correctly throughout — the 409 classifies as ambiguous (OPERATIONS_SPEC §2) so the reconciler owns it, and the transaction page keeps showing `pending / under review` rather than claiming a cancellation that has not happened.

**Some staging customers refuse payouts (same run):** `cus_033TR1SzDUnhK19QUbwArc` answers `403 CAPABILITY_SUSPENDED` — *"This account is restricted from initiating this money movement."* — on `POST /v2/payouts` despite an active, funded USD virtual account. `cus_033TljKNH86Bxo7mUeGIpx` works. The e2e tries funded accounts in turn rather than reading the first refusal as a broken route.
